canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the surveyed work, the prevailing usage treats helpfulness as a latent quality of model responses: being useful, relevant, informative, supportive, and satisfying relative to a user's query, instruction, or intent. Many papers state this in near-equivalent terms, sometimes adding directness, comprehensiveness, factual accuracy, or alignment with stated or implied goals. Smaller lines of work narrow it to basic task completion or instruction adherence, cast it as perceived helpfulness grounded in a user's own experience and satisfaction during collaboration, or define it through domain criteria such as culturally aware support, subjective advice quality shaped by personal or majority preferences, or tutor guidance that is constructive without giving the full answer. Some authors also use the neighboring term usefulness, either for direct answers to instructions or for retained task performance and compliant responses to benign requests, often alongside safety trade-offs.

Space of facets. Papers most often position helpfulness as one objective in multi-objective or human-preference alignment, commonly alongside harmlessness and sometimes honesty, humor, or a broader general standard. Within that umbrella, some papers spell out constituent criteria such as relevance, accuracy, insightfulness, quality, and comprehensiveness, while advice-focused work emphasizes empathy, actionability, creativity, practicality, and collective preferences, and culturally focused work describes 'culturally aware helpfulness' as support that respects cultural norms. The term also overlaps with instruction following in several places: one benchmark defines helpfulness as completing the basic task in the instruction, and another rates 'helpfulness & instruction-following' together, so papers do not always reserve the name for the same level of abstraction.

Space of measurement. Papers link helpfulness to 37 measurement instruments and 7 behavioral indicators, using a mix of preference datasets, general benchmarks, human evaluation, and judge models. The most common operationalizations are HH-RLHF, LLM-as-a-judge, MT-Bench, Human evaluation, and PKU-SafeRLHF: in practice, helpfulness is read off pairwise preference labels and win rates, GPT-4 style ratings on fixed scales or binary judgments, and benchmark aggregates for dialogue or general capability. These choices often mirror the dominant definition of useful and relevant assistance, but some papers operationalize helpfulness differently, for example as accuracy on GSM8K or XNLI/X-CSQA, Not-Overrefusal Rate, zero-shot task performance, or multimodal benchmark performance.

Links. Across 17 linked constructs, harmlessness is the recurring counterpart: many papers say it is related to helpfulness, usually as a trade-off, tension, or competing objective, and some report negative correlation, including on HH-RLHF and SafeRLHF. Several papers claim a causal relationship from alignment and safety alignment to helpfulness, while one paper on safety tuning states that the causal relationship runs in a negative direction for helpfulness. At the behavioral level, papers claim causal relationships from refusal and overrefusal to helpfulness, with refusal described as rendering a response unhelpful.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across the surveyed work, the prevailing usage treats helpfulness as a latent quality of model responses: being useful, relevant, informative, supportive, and satisfying relative to a user's query, instruction, or intent. Many papers state this in near-equivalent terms, sometimes adding directness, comprehensiveness, factual accuracy, or alignment with stated or implied goals. Smaller lines of work narrow it to basic task completion or instruction adherence, cast it as perceived helpfulness grounded in a user's own experience and satisfaction during collaboration, or define it through domain criteria such as culturally aware support, subjective advice quality shaped by personal or majority preferences, or tutor guidance that is constructive without giving the full answer. Some authors also use the neighboring term usefulness, either for direct answers to instructions or for retained task performance and compliant responses to benign requests, often alongside safety trade-offs.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Papers most often position helpfulness as one objective in multi-objective or human-preference alignment, commonly alongside harmlessness and sometimes honesty, humor, or a broader general standard. Within that umbrella, some papers spell out constituent criteria such as relevance, accuracy, insightfulness, quality, and comprehensiveness, while advice-focused work emphasizes empathy, actionability, creativity, practicality, and collective preferences, and culturally focused work describes 'culturally aware helpfulness' as support that respects cultural norms. The term also overlaps with instruction following in several places: one benchmark defines helpfulness as completing the basic task in the instruction, and another rates 'helpfulness & instruction-following' together, so papers do not always reserve the name for the same level of abstraction.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link helpfulness to 37 measurement instruments and 7 behavioral indicators, using a mix of preference datasets, general benchmarks, human evaluation, and judge models. The most common operationalizations are HH-RLHF, LLM-as-a-judge, MT-Bench, Human evaluation, and PKU-SafeRLHF: in practice, helpfulness is read off pairwise preference labels and win rates, GPT-4 style ratings on fixed scales or binary judgments, and benchmark aggregates for dialogue or general capability. These choices often mirror the dominant definition of useful and relevant assistance, but some papers operationalize helpfulness differently, for example as accuracy on GSM8K or XNLI/X-CSQA, Not-Overrefusal Rate, zero-shot task performance, or multimodal benchmark performance.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: Across 17 linked constructs, harmlessness is the recurring counterpart: many papers say it is related to helpfulness, usually as a trade-off, tension, or competing objective, and some report negative correlation, including on HH-RLHF and SafeRLHF. Several papers claim a causal relationship from alignment and safety alignment to helpfulness, while one paper on safety tuning states that the causal relationship runs in a negative direction for helpfulness. At the behavioral level, papers claim causal relationships from refusal and overrefusal to helpfulness, with refusal described as rendering a response unhelpful.

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define helpfulness as the usefulness, relevance, or effectiveness of a model's output in addressing a user's query, instruction, needs, or goals. A few papers narrow this to particular settings such as tutoring, advice, accessibility, safety-limited compliance, or advertised task performance, but these are still scoped versions of the same core property of user-directed utility rather than different phenomena.
